source.note: Supplied by the project owner as the model NPC 3463 was built from. The modded build kept only a decomposed fftools.npc-build-assets.v1 dump of Otto, which has no AssetBundle container table, so export-logical-model-source resolves zero routes for him and the normal publisher can never see him.

corroboration.shader: npcs/3463__Otto/assets/objects/object_16__16.unityobj declares Shader "ToonShading_blendSrcalphaInvsrcalpha", the same ShaderLab program the published npc_rex uses, so its passes, render queue and declared texture defaults are Otto's own rather than a substitute.
corroboration.ramp: _ShaderMap binds the already published ToonRamp9.png, byte-identical to the copy beside npc_rex.

declaredDivergence.detail: Triangle 1501 (vertices 1210/1169/350) is wound against its authored normals; its cross-product length is 0.0037 and the normal alignment -0.00012, a near-degenerate sliver. --repair-winding flipped it and reported the numbers. Without the flag the tool only reports such triangles.

declaredDivergence.what: one animation clip instead of three
declaredDivergence.detail: The authored file carries a single track, Bip01Action.001 (183 channels, 5.86 s), published as stand1. Otto's decomposed dump holds stand1, stand2 and stand3; recovering the other two needs a parser for that authoring format.

declaredDivergence.what: texture provenance is the authored PNG
declaredDivergence.detail: An authored texture has no Unity byte stream, so the declared source chain is its own decoded RGBA8, recorded as RGBA32 with a single baseLevelOnly level. The published PNG keeps its top-left origin and decoded_rgba8 hashes the flipped buffer, because the runtime reverses vertical-flip-only-for-png-top-left-origin before comparing.

acceptance.validator: ffone_skinned_model::validate, the same one every published model passes
acceptance.gpu: status success, foreground coverage 8.9%, 1 skinned mesh, 1 material applied
acceptance.installedAs: npc/npc_otto (package route equals logicalName, so no alias is needed)

source.note: AudioClip payloads in these bundles are already Ogg Vorbis -- the content-pack cooker validates exactly that and emits the stream unchanged -- so nothing was transcoded.

transform.ownership: Two data sources decide it: the installed model logicalName and the m_strName of every m_pNanoData row whose m_iMesh selects that model. A clip belongs to a nano when its own name prefix normalises to one of those. Using only the model name hid Princess Bubblegum, whose clips are PBubblegum_*/P.Bubblegum_* after the table spelling P.Bubblegum rather than the registry spelling. The owner is the package route of the model, which is how the installed catalogue keys voice.

stillSilent.reason: nano_holonano is the unnamed placeholder nano that rows 39 and 40 select with an empty m_strName; nano_upgrade is a model no table row references at all - the string nano_upgrade does not appear in m_pNanoMeshData. Neither has a clip in the clean primary build, the academy donor or the patched build.
stillSilent.correction: nano_belladonnaN was listed here before in error: its model is installed as nano/nano_belladonna and its voice already exists under the owner nano_belladonna.

notes: install-semantic-audio could not be used: it keys on the project asset-manifest.json the native tree no longer carries, the same reason the equipment installers had to be replaced by narrow additive ones.
